response.justification: Broad, long-tenured engineer with genuine high-throughput distributed systems exposure (Sociomantic/dunnhumby: microservices handling millions of HTTP requests per second, low-latency async I/O) and current, directly relevant work on AI-agent infrastructure and MCP code generators at re:cinq. TypeScript is clearly strong, and the software-craftsmanship background (TDD, CI/CD, trunk-based development, open-source test tooling) fits the review-and-extend-AI-output model well. However, Python — an explicit must-have — is absent from the skills list and every role description, the deepest distributed-systems work is 6+ years old with recent roles skewing full-stack/product, and the resume shows little evidence of technical strategy at scale, cross-functional stakeholder management, or on-call/incident ownership. Worth a screen to probe Python depth and current systems-design ability, but not a clear yes on paper.
strengths: Proven high-throughput, low-latency microservices experience at ad-tech scale
Current hands-on AI-agent infrastructure and MCP tooling work
Strong TypeScript, testing rigor, and unusually wide technical breadth
concerns: No demonstrated Python experience despite it being a must-have
Distributed-systems depth is dated; recent roles are product/full-stack
Thin evidence of technical strategy, stakeholder management, and on-call ownership
